subject: Temporal dependency mapping & sample RTO/RPO evidence for SIG review
messages:
From: Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@archonbank.com>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.com; priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: ops-compliance@archonbank.com
Date: Sat, 03 Oct 2026 16:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporal dependency mapping & sample RTO/RPO evidence for SIG review

Hi Marcus and team,

Thanks for the materials you shared in the CAIQ questionnaire. For our SIG review we need a slightly different artifact set: specifically a temporal dependency mapping that shows service-level RTO/RPO dependencies (what must recover first to meet your stated RTOs), plus a small set of raw traces from one DR exercise to validate your warm-cache/kv rehydrate timings.

Can you provide: 
- a dependency map (visual + row-level breakdown) that ties services to RTO tiers and recovery order,
- sampled traces (10–20 request flows) from your most recent DR run showing KV warm-up times and end-to-end request latencies, and
- an index file that maps each trace to the component it exercises.

We can accept redacted traces but need timestamps and component tags. Goal: SIG reviewer wants to see temporal sequencing and that your stated RTOs are realistic given the warm-cache behaviors.

Target turnaround: can you get this to us by end of day Monday 10/05? If that’s tight, even a work-in-progress map + one trace will help.

Thanks,
Lydia Chen
Senior Manager, Operational Risk
Archon Bank — Compliance Ops

On Fri, Oct 2, 2026 at 09:01 AM PDT marcus.lin@redwood.com wrote:
> (previous thread headers omitted)
From: marcus.lin@redwood.com <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@archonbank.com>
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 03 Oct 2026 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporal dependency mapping & sample RTO/RPO evidence for SIG review

Hi Lydia — thanks for the clear ask. We’ll prioritize this.

Quick plan:
- I’ll own the dependency mapping (high-level swimlanes + row-level CSV) and will pull in Priyom for the runbook snippets.
- Neha will extract the DR traces and produce the index that maps trace IDs to components and timestamps.
- We’ll redact customer identifiers but keep exact timing metadata and component tags per your note.

Deliverables we’ll upload to a shared folder by end of day Monday (10/05):
1) redwood_temporal_map_v1.xlsx — a sheet per RTO tier with recovery order and short rationale
2) rto_rpo_test-traces.tar.gz — up to 20 trace samples (lightly redacted), each file named with a trace id and component set
3) evidence_index_readme.md — maps traces to the components and includes test-run metadata (time, scenario id, on-call lead)

Couple of clarifying questions so we scope the right set: 
- For the dependency map, do you want infrastructure (region/availability-zone) dependencies included or just application-service dependencies?
- For sampling, is there a preference for the run (production-like failover vs scheduled test)? We ran a scheduled multi-region cache-warm exercise on 2026-09-18 that matches what you want, but we also have a production incident replay from 2026-07-09.

If you confirm infra dependencies are useful and prefer the 9/18 run, we’ll use that test as the source.

I’ll post the upload link once the files are ready.

— Marcus Lin
Director, Production Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: priyom.das@redwood.com <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.com
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com, Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@archonbank.com>
Date: Sun, 04 Oct 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporal dependency mapping & sample RTO/RPO evidence for SIG review

Marcus — uploading the first pass now. Attaching the artifacts and a short readme. Notes below.

Attachments: redwood_temporal_map_v1.xlsx (attachment stub), rto_rpo_test-traces.tar.gz (attachment stub), evidence_index_readme.md (attachment stub)

Summary of what’s included in this upload:
- Temporal map: includes application-level dependencies and the infra-level groupings (region/az). Columns: service, rto_tier, recovery_order, depends_on, short_rationale. We included an appendix row that describes the failover trigger points we use to decide order.
- Traces: 12 sample flows from the 2026-09-18 scheduled warm-cache rehearsal. Each trace file includes timestamps and component tags (cache-init, api-gateway, model-host, kv-restore). All PII replaced with placeholders and client IDs hashed.
- Evidence index: matches each trace id to scenario id, node-set, test-run start/end, and the on-call owner. Also contains the raw kv-rehydrate timing summary we pulled (median/95th percentiles).

Quick highlights relevant to SIG:
- Median KV warm-up per node for the rehearsal was ~320ms; 95th was ~1.6s (this matches the RTO window claimed for our Tier 2 services).
- End-to-end median latency during the start-of-run period was 180ms; 95th spiked to 2.2s while a subset of model-host instances rehydrated kv.

Questions for the reviewer (Lydia):
1) Would you like the raw trace JSONs (full request/response) or the timestamped event logs only? We redacted payloads but can provide full events under an NDA if needed.
2) Do you require component-level resource utilization (CPU/GPU/mem) during the run, or only timing traces? We can add an extract if the SIG reviewer requests it.

I’ll stand by for a reply. If Lydia wants component resource metrics we can produce a focused extract by EOD.

— Priyom Das
Sr. Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@archonbank.com>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: ops-compliance@archonbank.com
Date: Sun, 04 Oct 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporal dependency mapping & sample RTO/RPO evidence for SIG review

Team — thanks for the quick turnaround and the artifacts. I reviewed the index and a few traces; this is the right level of detail. A couple of follow-ups before I pass to the SIG reviewer: 

1) Please include a one-paragraph statement that confirms whether any production traffic was replayed for the 09/18 run (you included that it was a scheduled rehearsal). We need explicit confirmation that no customer data was used beyond hashed ids.
2) For one trace (trace_09-18_007) the sequence shows a KV rehydrate >2s — can you add a short note on why this outlier occurred and whether it’s considered within your RTO acceptance criteria?

Once we have those two clarifications I’ll attach the files to the SIG packet. If you can add the short clarifications inline in the evidence_index_readme.md and re-upload, that will be fastest.

Appreciate the speed.

— Lydia
Senior Manager, Operational Risk
Archon Bank — Compliance Ops
